test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom/phrase from the options:**"Get your walking papers"**

options.text: Be fired or dismissed from a job

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e., **Be fired or dismissed from a job**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The phrase **"Get your walking papers"** means to be dismissed or fired from a job. (नौकरी से निकाला जाना) • **Example:** After the company’s downsizing decision, several employees received their walking papers. • This idiom is commonly used in informal contexts to indicate termination of employment. (अनौपचारिक संदर्भों में उपयोग किया जाता है) • Hence, the meaning of **"Get your walking papers"** is associated with being fired or dismissed. (निकाला जाना) • **Example:** He knew he would get his walking papers if he didn’t meet the sales targets. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e., **Be fired or dismissed from a job**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: Go on vacation** (छुट्टी पर जाना) • **Explanation:** Refers to taking a break from work or daily routines for leisure or travel. • **Example:** She decided to go on vacation after completing her project. • **Option 2: Receive a promotion** (पदोन्नति प्राप्त करना) • **Explanation:** Refers to being elevated to a higher position or rank in a job or organization. • **Example:** After years of hard work, he finally received a promotion to senior manager. • **Option 3: Be given permission to retire** (सेवानिवृत्त होने की अनुमति दी गई) • **Explanation:** Refers to being allowed or encouraged to stop working permanently due to age or other factors. • **Example:** After 30 years of service, she was given permission to retire with full benefits. 3e:T87f, The correct answer is **Option 1**.
